## Why

The public repository claimed three things that do not exist:

1. **An editorial board.** `docs/governance/governance-and-code-of-conduct.md`
   said "An editorial board exists, distinct from the technical
   maintainers" and routed contested claims, officer-naming concurrence
   and capture resistance through it (F-189). No board exists; SIG-GOV-015
   is waived for the interim (WV-02, ADR-164) in favour of a disclosed
   single-maintainer authority plus a public decision log.
2. **A counsel review / counsel document.** The same doc's legal-home
   scope note and reviewer gatekeeping cited "a counsel opinion (HG-02)"
   and "HG-02 counsel confirms the publication posture"; the source
   registry carried five `rights_reviewed_by = "counsel (HG-02)"` values;
   the publication checklist attributed dispositions to counsel at nine
   lines. ADR-167 records the truth: those determinations were the
   operator's own — **there was no counsel** (C-3, U-013); the counsel
   clauses are waived (WV-07, ADR-182).
3. **A served corrections/dispute mechanism.** The doc named "the served
   `/corrections` and `/dispute` mechanisms" — while the `/dispute/`
   page itself states the durable anonymous receiver is not yet
   operating (G2 0c); one-click unidentified intake is waived for Round
   11 (WV-05, ADR-180).

The same text also claimed the project is "not a public launch" and
"Go-public (GATE-G2) remains blocked" — the site has been public since
2026-09-16 — and marked a second reviewer "still owed" (waived for
Round-11 releases, WV-03, ADR-163).

## What this does

- **The false statements are struck in place, never deleted.** Each
  keeps `~~…~~` with a dated `*(struck 2026-10-03 — see Corrections;
  ADR-…)*` pointer — the earlier record stays legible as struck (the
  append-only way a document is corrected in the open). A new dated
  `## Corrections` section lands every pointer: it states the posture
  **only in the operator's own adopted sentences**, quoted verbatim
  from `RATIFICATION_LOG.md` with their round times (WV-01, WV-02,
  WV-03, WV-05, WV-07 — A-23, round 9, 2026-10-01T04:28:49Z; C-3,
  round 19, 2026-10-01T04:54:19Z), each labelled with its requirement
  and ADR (ADR-163/164/165/167/180/182). Everything else in the section
  is apparatus — bold labels, `:`-ended lead-ins, `—` pointer fragments.
- **C-5 holds.** No name, no description, no "who runs SIG" copy — the
  correction goes no further than the adopted WV-01 sentence; the
  2026-09-15 legal-home text is neither extended nor rewritten.
- **The five registry values read the fixed vocabulary verbatim:**
  `"the operator's own determination (no counsel)"` (ADR-167 decision 2
  — not "operator-reported"). Nothing else in those entries changed: no
  date, no `ingestion_permitted`, and the dated `notes` records stay
  byte-identical history.
- **The publication checklist is corrected by append (OM-13).** A dated
  `## 2026-10-03 — correction` section names every counsel-claim line
  (:9, :13, :29, :48, :51, :84, :144, :164, :176), quotes C-3 verbatim,
  and cites WV-07/ADR-182 + the registry re-recording; the body is not
  rewritten. Operator words quoted inside dated records (:75, :251)
  stay verbatim — they record what was said; the correction records who
  made the determinations.
- **`contributor-onboarding-usability-study.md`'s counsel-review claim**
  is struck in place with the same dated pointer.

## Copy (B-2)

Eleven agent-drafted rows appended **pending** to `batch-01.md` —
`GC-01…GC-09`, `GC-11`. GC-01…03 are ADR-164's E2-03 drafted wording
verbatim ("SIG does not yet have an editorial board…"); GC-04/05 and
the combined GC-06 are ADR-167's pinned publication-basis forms — the
row sha256s equal the ADR-recorded `f62f9e98…` and `c7e4f78b…`;
GC-07…09 and GC-11 are record candidates. Per the contract ("every new
sentence is confirmed in copy batch #1 or absent"), **none of these is
in the doc** — they land only on the operator's verbatim confirmation at
a copy-batch sitting. The binding test asserts every row is `pending`,
sha256-verified and absent from the doc.

## Tests

`tests/unit/test_p34_16_repo_honesty.py` (9 tests — fail if the false
claims return):

- no `rights_reviewed_by` value names counsel; exactly the five ADR-167
  entries carry the fixed vocabulary, `rights_reviewed_on` and
  `ingestion_permitted` untouched;
- no board/counsel claim survives in `docs/governance/**` outside
  struck, quoted or correction context (enumerated honest contexts only —
  disclosure of absence, conditional future, supersession, the
  hostile-reader dossier's role-play of the *documented organisation's*
  counsel);
- every struck statement keeps `~~…~~` + a dated pointer; the Corrections
  section is dated, cites the four ADRs and quotes the six adopted
  sentences verbatim, apparatus-only outside them;
- no "who runs SIG" section; the legal-home text byte-identical;
- the checklist correction is appended, dated, naming ADR-167/182;
- GC-* rows pending, sha256-verified, absent from the doc.
  Red proof: reverting the doc + registry to `8365dae8` fails 6 tests.

## Boundaries

- No production mutation; no live leg; public `main` keeps the old text
  until the operator merges (OP-08).
- No `ingestion_permitted` flip and no `HG-nn` tick; the registry diff is
  exactly the five `rights_reviewed_by` lines.
- Append-only everywhere: strikes keep the struck text; the checklist
  body is untouched; batch-01 only gains rows; no landed ADR body edited;
  dated `notes` records (which mention the former counsel attribution
  inside a dated FLIPPED record) stay byte-identical — they record what
  was recorded then.
- GC-* rows are `pending` — the agent never confirms; confirmation is
  the operator's words at a copy-batch sitting (OM-07/08).
- Diff budget: 7 files + this run ledger (well under the ≤1,500 ceiling).
